purpose: Platform/weapon capability routing layer that prevents historical-baseline bias, platform-class underestimation, and omission of branch-specific or ahistorical systems. It is a review index, not an OOB: actual presence/readiness still comes from checkpoint/event-local state.
principles: Historical reputation or historical combat outcome is never a substitute for current-branch capability evidence.

A new or divergent system is assessed from its declared engineering/operational properties, maturity, availability, crew/training and mission fit; do not snap it back to the nearest historical weapon.
Platform capability is multi-stage. Submarines are not reduced to torpedo hit rate; surface combatants are not reduced to gun caliber or first-salvo firepower.
An indexed capability is a candidate capability, not proof that every participating unit possesses it. Match class/configuration and actual committed units before applying.
Unknown novelty is explicit. A runtime-declared AHISTORICAL_NEW/DIVERGENT/UNKNOWN system without a capability record and provenance keeps final combat adjudication unready.

platform_classes.label: Submarine force and underwater combat system
anti_underestimate_rules: Do not score submarines only by sinkings or torpedo hit probability.
Count the probability chain sortie→station→contact→position→attack→survive→re-sortie and the value of reconnaissance/contact reporting.
For 潜高/high-speed submerged boats, evaluate threshold crossing from stale contact to firing position; never treat 18–20 kt as continuous silent patrol speed.
Operational patrol power and enemy diversion can be materially stronger even when individual torpedo performance is unchanged.

strength_anchors: Conventional mature classes: typical +8–9% surface range, +7–10% submerged endurance, reduced dive/maintenance variance; apply through mission-state probabilities, not one multiplier.
First-generation 潜高: 18.5–19.0 kt submerged maximum with about 55–65 min full-speed budget; main combat value is deliberate underwater repositioning.
Settled 1943-spring source evaluates effective patrol power around 1.4–1.6× historical branch baseline; this is an operational ledger anchor, not an automatic future combat multiplier.

platform_classes.label: Surface combatant force
anti_underestimate_rules: Do not score a surface ship only by nominal displacement, gun caliber or historical reputation.
Use practical speed/range, reliability, damage-state transitions, tracking/fire-control and formation tactics.
Japanese first-line destroyer/cruiser torpedo capability includes the probability of converting carried reloads into a second effective salvo in prolonged actions; it is not merely first-salvo tubes.
Radar early contact and optical/torpedo follow-up are separate causal stages; one does not erase the other.

strength_anchors: Asashio/Kagero lineage has higher practical schedule reliability and range; Kagero full-load practical maximum around 34.6–34.9 kt and ~5,300 nmi/18 kt in the technical baseline.
Mature equipped units can reach a first-launch→second-effective-salvo cycle in roughly 12–20 min under suitable conditions; never convert this into double instantaneous firepower.
Damage-control/reserve-margin improvements can preserve mission function after non-catastrophic hits and must be modeled as state-transition effects.

anti_underestimate_rules: Treat carrier capability as hull+deck cycle+ready air group+crew+mission geometry, not nominal aircraft capacity.

platform_classes.label: ASW/escort combat system
anti_underestimate_rules: ASW improvement acts first through search→datum→delivery opportunities; do not multiply sinkings directly by detection gain.

platform_classes.label: Land weapon/formation system
anti_underestimate_rules: New land weapons require explicit capability and maturity records; do not inherit historical unit effectiveness automatically.

platform_classes.label: Special or branch-original weapon system
anti_underestimate_rules: A historically absent system has no historical combat-result prior. Resolve from mechanism and current-branch evidence.
A prototype or paper design is not a combat unit; availability/readiness gates are mandatory.

systems.rule: Use branch variant performance/configuration when the participating unit is this line; do not silently substitute historical Sakae-Zero data.
Treat as a divergent carrier attack-aircraft configuration subject to actual surviving units and replacement state.

systems.designation: 潜高 first-generation high-speed submerged submarine
systems.rule: Evaluate underwater repositioning, battery budget, information age and readiness. Never downgrade it to historical 8-kt-class submarine movement or upgrade it to continuous silent 19-kt pursuit.

systems.rule: This branch-original development is reviewable when encountered but must not be counted as present/ready solely because the design exists. Require OOB/readiness evidence.
Review first salvo, reload, recontact and re-entry as a cycle. Do not cap Japanese destroyer/cruiser threat at initial tube count.
Apply practical speed/range/reliability/damage-state effects to matching ships; do not infer a generic fleetwide bonus.
Resolve boat+aircraft+crew+launch/recovery+mission package as one readiness chain; count only the checkpoint-confirmed ready subset.
Apply as increased datum localization/weapon-delivery opportunities in covered lanes, not as a direct sink-rate multiplier.

runtime_registration_rule: Any event-local weapon/platform not safely represented by a listed system may be supplied under combat input weapon_systems. If historical_relation is AHISTORICAL_NEW, DIVERGENT_VARIANT, AHISTORICAL_TIMING or UNKNOWN, capability_record and provenance are mandatory before final combat adjudication.
